Subject: Re: PayGrid model fit eval - next steps & parity thresholds

Hi Samir -

Great to meet you and Alyssa on the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned:

1) Summary of discovery
- Primary goal: replace PayGrid's current proprietary classifier for payment intent with an open-model based stack to reduce licensing costs and get faster iteration.
- Success metrics: intent classification F1 parity (>=95% of baseline) and <2% regression on high-risk route detection.
- Non-functional requirements: p95 latency <= 120ms for text-only inference; throughput ~200 rps per shard.

2) Redwood recommended starting point (per call)
- Candidate open models: open-13B-quant (7-bit), open-7B-quant (4-bit) for faster inference.
- Redwood proprietary baseline for comparison: redwood-prod-13b (our internal tuned baseline).
- Suggested acceptance thresholds: 95% intent parity (F1), <2% delta on high-risk false negatives, and acceptable latency/cost envelope.

3) Eval assets we will provide
- Initial benchmark report (see attached) with house metrics on similarity tasks and a short evaluation harness.
- Prompt sets: we'll share the exact prompt variations and negative examples you flagged (attached).
- Notebook: lightweight, reproducible eval that runs model inference on your 5k holdout set.

4) Risks / quality regression concerns
- Tokenization mismatches on edge cases (amounts, currencies) may cause precision drops - we'll include token-level diagnostics.
- Calibration drift: some open variants need prompt tuning to match decision thresholds; expect a small tuning window.

5) Proposed timeline & mutual action plan
- This week (W1): we deliver benchmark PDF + prompt sets and a readme on running the eval (you'll get access to the Drive link).
- Next week (W2): Redwood runs a parity eval on your holdout set and shares per-case diffs; we'll also provide a latency/cost projection.
- W3: Alignment call to review results and agree on canary rollout plan.

Please confirm the holdout dataset id you want us to use (you mentioned pg_holdout_v3) and whether you want us to include language variants beyond US English.

Attachments: paygrid_benchmark_report_v1.pdf, paygrid_prompt_sets_v1.xlsx

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Solutions - Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

Lauren / Marissa - forwarding a quick internal note after I ran a 1k sample through the open-7B-quant and redwood-prod-13b to set expectations.

--- forwarded message ---
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 08:21:00 -0800
Subject: PayGrid quick bench notes

Summary (1k sample, balanced classes):
- redwood-prod-13b: Intent F1 = 0.892; High-risk false negative rate = 0.038; p95 latency (128 token avg) = 95ms; est cost per 1k tokens = $0.62
- open-7B-quant: Intent F1 = 0.865; High-risk false negative rate = 0.051; p95 latency (128 token avg) = 65ms; est cost per 1k tokens = $0.18
- open-13B-quant (7-bit): Intent F1 = 0.885; High-risk FN = 0.041; p95 latency = 85ms; est cost per 1k tokens = $0.34

Notes:
- open-7B-quant shows a ~3% absolute drop vs baseline on F1 and higher FN on high-risk cases - within a tunable window if we invest prompt engineering and short-domain fine-tuning.
- Tokenization issues centered on monetary strings - recommend a small preproc step (normalizing currency tokens) before inference.
- For PayGrid's target of >=95% parity, we should plan either: (a) open-13B-quant + prompt tuning, or (b) open-7B-quant + short-domain-adapt (3-5k steps) to close the last gap.

Attached: paygrid_prompt_sets_v1.xlsx (prompt variations + negative examples)

Aditya
Senior ML Engineer - Redwood Inference
